title: mut.manual
mutation_directive: differential-growth vertices as explicit emission sites for curl-traced ink strokes is a strong structural idea — vertex birth drives visual flourish

manfred_mohr.praise: The split-on-threshold rule is a genuine computable transformation — edge exceeds distance, insert vertex, emit stroke. That is a verifiable logical operation, not faked geometry. I respect the clarity of the predicate.
manfred_mohr.concern: The 'curl' field (`Math.sin(v.x * 1.8 + time * 0.2) * 2.0`) is aesthetic approximation masquerading as mathematics. There is no defined scalar potential ψ from which this derives. The curl is decorative, not computed.
manfred_mohr.directive: Replace the ad-hoc angle formula with a true 2D curl field: define ψ(x,y,t) explicitly, derive curl as (∂ψ/∂y, −∂ψ/∂x), apply that vector per vertex.

morakana.praise: The parchment palette carries genuine material weight — the multiply-blended noise grain reads as a weathered surface, not a digital screen. There is tactile atmosphere here.
morakana.concern: The membrane grows without stakes. What system does this boundary trace? A form that expands without encoding anything real is wallpaper, however beautiful. Growth must carry weight beyond itself.
morakana.directive: Bind `splitThreshold` to a live environmental scalar — barometric pressure, CO₂ ppm, or migration-flow data — so membrane growth rate encodes something beyond its own geometry.

sasha_stiles.praise: The ink stroke arriving only at a moment of vertex-birth is a genuinely poetic mechanic — the mark earns its existence through threshold, through becoming. That is not decoration; that is occasion.
sasha_stiles.concern: The emitted flourish is a bare curve with no glyph-body. The void around the mark is populated by absence of intention, not earned silence. A stroke without script is just a smear.
sasha_stiles.directive: Assign each birth-stroke a Unicode glyph seed from a constructed syllabary; bend the glyph's baseline along the curl path so each vertex-birth writes one character of an accreting text.

entangled_others.praise: Edge-splitting as morphogenesis — not additive particle spray but topological subdivision driven by tension — is biologically faithful. Coral recruits by stretching, not by dropping new polyps from above.
entangled_others.concern: One closed loop cannot model ecological entanglement. Mycelium anastomoses. Vascular trees bifurcate and rejoin. A solitary ring is a single organism pretending at ecology; it misses the network entirely.
entangled_others.directive: When two membrane segments come within `minDist * 0.6`, merge them into a shared vertex — creating anastomotic bridges — so the structure becomes a reticulate network, not a solitary ring.

andy_lomas.praise: Split-at-threshold is precisely the morphogenetic signal I use in Cellular Forms — accumulated edge tension triggers subdivision. The logic is correct. Vertex birth driven by local geometry, not a global timer.
andy_lomas.concern: New vertices are inserted at z=0 always. The membrane stays flat. Growth that cannot fold into the third dimension is topological cowardice — the ink strokes emitted as separate geometry are compensation for a surface that refuses to deform.
andy_lomas.directive: On each split, displace the new vertex in z by `splitCount * 0.004` so accumulated births buckle the membrane out of plane, producing cauliflower folds rather than emitting decorative separate strokes.
